body:
# ISSUE-UNWIRED-BUDGETS-AND-RECOVERY

Found by the #1100 wiring audit (`engine/.pi/architecture/wiring-claims.md`, rows W13/W14), which now fails the build if either gap is quietly re-described as wired.

## W13 — the budget enforcer is never constructed

| element | state |
|---|---|
| `ExecutionEnforcerImpl` + counters + presets | present, tested |
| `evaluate_tool_call` callers outside `engine/src/enforcement/` | **none** |
| composition roots (CLI, Action, MCP) | never construct it |

Consequence: `hard_limit`, `soft_warning_threshold`, `max_calls` and the autonomy presets are configured, validated and echoed — and consulted by nothing at dispatch. `README.md` §1 previously claimed "every execution runs inside … budget boundaries"; it now says which controls run (risk gating, permissions, capacity ledger) and which do not.

`enforcement_preset` is threaded through `RunInput` → builder and never read to build an enforcer, so a caller can pass `--enforcement aggressive` and get exactly the default behaviour.

## W14 — recovery recipes are never switched on

`service_impl/node.rs` consults `self.recovery_service` on failure; `with_recovery_service` has no caller, so the field is always `None` and no recipe runs.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed in the audit

Wiring either one changes behaviour at dispatch: the enforcer would start refusing calls that exceed a configured budget, and recipes would start executing recovery steps on failure. That needs a decision (which config arms them, what the default is) and an acceptance test that shows the refusal happens **before** the tool runs — not a doc edit. #1100 deliberately recorded the gaps instead of guessing.

## Acceptance

1. Decide per module: wire it, or delete it. A control that cannot be switched on has to be one of those two; "documented as unwired" is a holding pattern, not an answer.
2. If wired: the budget refusal must happen before the tool call (same place as the capacity gate), with a test that the tool's side effect never occurs.
3. Promote rows W13/W14 in `wiring-claims.tsv` to CONFIRMED in the same PR — the guard fails if a GAP row starts passing without the row being promoted.
4. If deleted: remove the module, its docs and its tests, and say so in the changelog.
title: enforcement/recovery: two modules are implemented, tested, and constructed by no entry point

body:
# ISSUE-DOC-CLAIMS-WIRING-AUDIT

## Why this exists

This series produced a repeating failure: **code that exists, compiles, passes its own tests, and is
never reached.**

| instance | how it was found |
|---|---|
| capacity ledger entirely unwired | the module doc had no EnforcementSeam component, so no wiring was ever planned |
| effect-scope oracle disabled in all 3 roots | reading the module doc against the entry points; #1072 was then closed COMPLETED anyway |
| drain shared no controls | a second ingestion path that owned none of the pipeline |
| drain backoff never persisted | the local mutation existed, the store write did not |

None of these is a compile error, a test failure, or a type mismatch. Each is a **claim of wiring that
was true of the code in isolation and false of the system.**

## The check that would have caught them

| method | finds | misses |
|---|---|---|
| grep for a symbol | the code exists | that nothing calls it |
| test suite | the tested path | an untested sibling path |
| reading the doc | what the doc says | whether it is true |
| **call graph, per claim** | **whether anything reaches it** | nothing relevant here |

Reachability is a graph property. The graph is the only tool in this repo that answers it, and it was
not part of any documentation review.

## Deliverable

A table per document:

| doc | claim | verdict | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| \`modules/capacity-ledger.md\` | "reserve precedes dispatch" | CONFIRMED | \`impact(capacity_verdict, upstream)\` → dispatch.rs:229 |
| \`modules/approval.md\` | "effect scope is verified" | **GAP** | no entry point sets \`approval_repo_path\` (#…) |
| \`ADR-0xx\` | "implemented end to end" | **DELETE** | claim removed; half was deferred |

Plus \`.pi/scripts/validate-wiring-claims.sh\`, which re-resolves each CONFIRMED row and fails when
the evidence disappears — so the audit decays visibly instead of silently.
title: audit: verify every module doc and ADR claim of end-to-end wiring against the call graph, then fix or delete what does not hold
